inline_text:
Closes #30.

This PR replaces the gateway enforcement bullet in Section 3.1 of the best practices guide with two bullets.

- **Enforce at the hooks.** Describes the runtime hooks as the enforcement point: the points across the lifecycle of a run where the runtime stops and hands the pending action to policy code, together with the context that led to it. Points to Section 4 for how the decision is made.
- **Use the gateway as a checkpoint.** Describes the MCP gateway as the control on the network path: one endpoint for remote MCP servers, OAuth, per-tool permission policy, and payload capture for the Section 6 action events. States its scope and how it works together with the hook.

Other changes in the same commit:

- The vendor name is out of the body. The Section 7 table keeps its row.
- agentgateway is named as an AAIF project in the body and in the Section 7 row.
- The Last Modified date for the guide in deliverables/README.md is updated, per deliverables/AGENTS.md.

The change touches Section 3.1, one row in the Section 7 table, and the README date, so it does not overlap with #36.

Disclosure: I co-lead the spec workstream of the OWASP Agent Control Standard, and I work at Capsule Security, which runs the hooks.security registry. Neither is cited in this change.

@MatthewKhouzam @flucktemberg-sap this is the PR requested on #30.
